_comment: What service-kit/ci/deploy_env.py reads from SSM Parameter Store or Secrets Manager
before the deploy job pushes an image, and hands to serverless (and to the rollback)
without ever writing the values into the workflow. Service-owned, like the rest of
deploy/: the kit script is byte-identical everywhere, these names are not.
Every ${env:NAME} in deploy/iac/serverless.yml that carries no default must be either
declared here or set by the deploy step itself, never both. The step sets IMAGE_URI
and LISTENER_RULE_PRIORITY, which is this service's own row in the service directory.
The two declared below are the estate's: the internal-edge stack publishes the shared
listener's ARN and the private zone's suffix under /foundry/<Stage>/network/, so no
service types either into a repository variable. {stage} is the deploy's target
environment, so the edge stack's Stage must be the same word. Where that stack is not
applied, the deploy job stops at its check step, before the push, naming both.
A service that needs a secret adds, for example:
"DATABASE_URL": {"secretsmanager": "<service>/{stage}/database-url"}
"AUTH_ISSUER":  {"ssm": "/<service>/{stage}/auth-issuer"}
An id may also name an EARLIER ssm variable as {NAME}, resolved in declaration
order, so a product-neutral service can build its reads on one declared prefix:
"COMMS_DEPLOYMENT":   {"ssm": "/comms/{stage}/deployment"}
"COMMS_EVENTS_QUEUE": {"ssm": "/{COMMS_DEPLOYMENT}/core/events-queue-arn"}
A service that sets custom.callerVpc to estate in serverless.yml declares the two
variables deploy/iac/caller_vpc.yml reads. scripts/check_service_iac.sh refuses
estate without them, and declared, an absent or empty one stops the job before the
push:
"ESTATE_CALLER_SG_ID": {"ssm": "/foundry/{stage}/network/estate-caller-sg-id"}
"PRIVATE_SUBNET_IDS":  {"ssm": "/foundry/{stage}/network/private-subnet-ids"}
The internal-edge stack publishes the first. The foundation network root publishes
the second, a comma-separated list of the VPC's private subnets.
The deploy role needs read access to each named parameter or secret; creating them
is an owner action, not this file's.
